newsitem.title: USA: Congress looking at ways to cut auto insurance.
newsitem.headline: Congress looking at ways to cut auto insurance.

text.p: U.S. drivers could save up to $225 million over a five-year period under a proposal by the Joint Economic Committee of Congress to lower automobile insurance premiums, the panel's chairman said on Monday.

Representative Jim Saxton, a New Jersey Republican, said "better government, laws, policies and regulations could cut insurance premiums by an average of $200 a year," per policy or 30 percent annually.
In a statement, Saxton said increased litigation costs had driven up the cost of car insurance, reduced incentives for auto safety developments, and pushed up medical costs.
The Joint Economic Committee proposed a plan to lower premiums by allowing individuals to select from several new types of insurance coverage.
The plan would allow consumers to change to "first party" coverage, which means they would only need to insure against injury to themselves and their own property.
Saxton said the proposal would especially benefit lower income families.
He said hearings and a report on the matter were planned soon.
